title: Suggestion Apply Orchestrator with Validation Playbook and Gated Canary
creator: Aisha Nadar
description: Build an orchestration component (Suggestion Apply Orchestrator) that can safely auto-apply Optimize's batching and caching recommendations with configurable gated rollouts, canary sizing, automated validation probes, and auditable rollback behavior. This ticket drives the server-side implementation + API + operator playbook for safe auto-apply, not the Console UX polish. Goal: reduce operator overhead for low-risk recommendations while guaranteeing recovery and explainability for regressions.
acceptance_criteria: API endpoint to submit a suggested Optimize config apply request that supports dry-run and immediate apply modes
Config apply runs through a gating pipeline: dry-run -> shadow -> small canary -> ramp -> full apply
Automated validation probes (latency, p95; cost delta; model quality proxies) run at each stage and can veto or trigger automatic rollback
Operators can attach manual approval steps between pipeline stages; approvals recorded in audit logs
Rollback reason and a minimal diff excerpt produced and persisted to audit trail for every revert
Metrics emitted for every apply attempt: canary_size, validation_results, decision_events, duration, and rollback_trigger
Support for tenant-scoped applies (per-customer) and global namespace applies with separate policies
End-to-end test harness that replays historical traces (production-sampled token distributions) to validate rollout logic
Documentation and an runbook/incident-playbook for investigating failed applies and performing manual rollbacks
technical_notes: Pipeline stages will be implemented as idempotent state transitions in the apply orchestration service (kafka-backed event-sourced state machine)
Validation probes: latency p50/p95/p99, error-rate, tokens/sec, per-token cost estimate. Quality proxies: hallucination detectors and rerank-based BLEU-like score on sampled prompt set.
Shadow stage: duplicate live traffic to candidate config but do not serve responses; collect metrics to compare against baseline with A/B microbatching
Canary sizing recommendation: use adaptive formula based on tenant traffic volume; floor 0.5% global traffic, ceiling 5% unless tenant-level apply requested

Rollback triggers are threshold-based and configurable per-policy. Default triggers: p95 latency increase > 20% OR error rate increase > 0.5% OR cost saving < 0 (i.e., negative savings) OR quality proxy drop > 5%
Explainable rollback record includes the minimal set of config keys changed, primer on why threshold tripped, and sample traces that failed validation
Security: all applies must include initiator identity and run under RBAC check; audit events persisted to customer-managed KMS-backed store for Private deployments
Storage: use existing rollout-ops table with new columns for suggestion_id, stage, validation_summary, and revert_metadata
Integrations: Console will call the apply API; console approval UX flows map to orchestration service webhook endpoints
Backwards compatibility: keep legacy manual apply endpoint; new orchestrator accepts legacy payloads and enriches with policy defaults
implementation_plan: Design API contract and JSON schema for suggestion apply request (dry_run, policy_id, tenant_scope, approval_required)
Implement orchestration state machine and persistence layer; add event hooks for validation probes
Add probe implementations: latency probe, cost estimator probe, quality-proxy probe, error-rate probe
Implement shadowing adapter that can tap a configurable percentage of traffic and forward to candidate runtime without affecting production responses
Add automatic rollback engine with pluggable threshold evaluators and tolerant cooldown windows
Create audit trail schema and hook KMS-backed encryption for Private deployments
Wire Console approval webhooks and the API for manual approval gates
Add telemetry to Redwood Console / Datadog: counters, histograms, traces for each apply attempt
Write end-to-end tests and a trace-replay harness to validate behavior under representative traffic patterns
Staged rollout to infra namespaces: staging -> canary infra -> prod with feature flag gated by release flag optimize.orchestrator.enabled
rollout_plan: Feature flag off by default. Deploy service behind optimize.orchestrator.enabled=false
Smoke deploy to staging, run synthetic probe suite on historical traces
Enable in 1% of infra traffic for internal test tenants and run 72h validation
Enable in 5% of infra traffic and allow automated ramp to 25% if no triggers for 24h
Open manual approval gate in Console for cross-team review before global enable
After 7 days of stable runs and sign-off, set default policy for low-risk suggestions to auto-apply with standard gates
Post-release: monitor cost savings and false-positive rollback rate for 30 days; tune thresholds and canary policies
risks: Undetected model-quality regressions from batching/quantization that our proxies miss -> potential user-facing quality issues
Too-aggressive auto-apply could cause oscillation in costs/latency if thresholds are mis-calibrated
Shadowing overhead may increase infra load and metric noise; must cap and backpressure
Permissions mistakes could allow unauthorised applies; RBAC checks must be enforced and audited
Large-scale rollouts without effective rollback could amplify failures across many tenants
qa_test_plan: Unit tests for state machine transitions and idempotence
Integration tests for probe pipeline using test runtime that mimics varying latencies and error patterns
Replay-based end-to-end tests: run historical traces with both baseline and candidate configs and assert validation outcomes
Chaos test: inject transient slowdowns and errors to ensure rollback triggers and cooldowns behave as expected
Manual runbook dry-runs: PM/Eng run a staged apply in staging and verify audit logs and explainability payloads
Security review checklist: RBAC scenarios, KMS encryption, and audit export validations
